docRequirement: `troubleshooting.md` line 39 binds the memory-recovery path to a user-runnable command: "If memory usage stays high after these steps, run `/heapdump` to write a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to `~/Desktop`. On Linux without a Desktop folder, the files are written to your home directory." Line 41 fixes the two artifacts and the breakdown's contents: "The breakdown shows resident set size, JS heap, array buffers, and unaccounted native memory, which helps identify whether the growth is in JavaScript objects or in native code. To inspect retainers, open the `.heapsnapshot` file in Chrome DevTools under Memory -> Load; the breakdown is the file ending in `-diagnostics.json`." Line 44 (Warning) fixes the privacy contract: "The `.heapsnapshot` file contains every string in the process. Don't attach it to a public issue or share it. Attach only the `-diagnostics.json` file when reporting a memory issue ... That file contains memory statistics and no conversation content or credentials." So: one command, two files in `~/Desktop` (home fallback), a `.heapsnapshot` V8 snapshot, and a `-diagnostics.json` carrying exactly the four counters and nothing else. Steps 1-4 of the same section are already satisfied here (`/compact` exists at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/slash-command-actions.ts:56, `--safe-mode` at apps/cli/src/index.ts:129) — only the heapdump step is unbuilt.
current: Nothing writes a heap snapshot anywhere in the fork, and no surface offers to. (1) Absence, NUL-safe: `grep -rai 'heapdump|heap_dump|writeHeapSnapshot|heapsnapshot' packages apps scripts docs-site --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs' --include='*.json' --include='*.md'` returns zero hits; no production file imports `node:v8` or `node:inspector` (`grep -rai "from 'v8'|from 'node:v8'|require('v8')|node:inspector" packages apps scripts` -> zero). (2) The desktop slash-command surface has no memory command: the id union at apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx:17 is `PermissionMode | CustomSlashCommandId | 'agents' | 'automations' | 'compact' | 'context' | 'create-skill' | 'create-plugin' | 'export' | 'init' | 'memory' | 'model' | 'clear' | 'help' | 'subtask' | 'usage'` (`'memory'` there is session MEMORY.md — slash-command-menu.tsx:176-180, dispatched to `openMemory` at slash-command-actions.ts:114-117 — not process memory), `featureCommands` at :225-240 lists those fourteen, and the dispatcher at slash-command-actions.ts:76-148 has no diagnostic branch. (3) The agent-callable slash allowlist is `new Set(['compact', 'help'])` — packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/slash-command.ts:10. (4) The CLI has no such command: the help text at apps/cli/src/index.ts:2043-2075 lists `run`, `doctor`, `plugin …`, `ping`, `health`, `versions`, `workspaces`, `sessions`, `connections`, `sources`, `session …`; `health` is `credentials:healthCheck` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:305-309) and `doctor` is scoped read-only to configuration by construction (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:1-24 docblock) and reports nothing about memory. (5) The nearest existing memory read is three counters over RPC, not a dump: packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/server.ts:58 does `const mem = process.memoryUsage()` and returns `memory: { heapUsed, heapTotal, rss }` on `server:getStatus`, typed at packages/core/src/types/server.ts:25-29; :123-131 adds a pass/fail check at 1.5 GB heap in `getHealthCheck`. `arrayBuffers` and `external` are read nowhere in the repo (`grep -rn -a 'arrayBuffers|mem.external' packages apps` -> zero), so even the four documented buckets have no partial coverage. (6) No wire channel exists to ask for one: the `server` namespace in packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts:11-19 holds eight channels (`getWorkspaces`, `createWorkspace`, `getStatus`, `getHealth`, `getActiveSessions`, `shuttingDown`, `statusChanged`, `homeDir`). (7) The one debug affordance that could host it is dev-only: apps/electron/src/main/menu.ts:193 gates the Debug submenu on `!app.isPackaged`, and its three items are update-check, install-update and a reset-to-defaults message box (:196-227), so a packaged build has no diagnostic menu at all.
divergence: The whole mechanism is missing, not a renamed field: no `/heapdump` command on any surface (desktop slash menu, CLI, agent-callable allowlist), no V8 snapshot writer, no `-diagnostics.json` breakdown, and no `~/Desktop`/home output path. Two secondary deltas matter for the fix. (a) Shape: the only memory data we produce is `ServerStatus.memory = { heapUsed, heapTotal, rss }` (packages/core/src/types/server.ts:25-29) — three counters delivered over RPC to a caller that never displays them, where the doc requires four buckets (resident set size, JS heap, array buffers, unaccounted native memory) persisted to a file; `arrayBuffers`/`external` are not even sampled, so the JS-versus-native discrimination the doc says the breakdown exists for is impossible today. (b) Process topology: Claude Code dumps the single CLI process, while here the memory can grow in the Electron main (which hosts SessionManager and the Pi client in-process) or in the Pi agent subprocess, so a faithful implementation has to name which process each artifact came from — a decision the page does not make for us.

change.what: New writer. Resolve the output directory exactly as the doc states: `join(homedir(), 'Desktop')` when it exists, else `homedir()`; return which one was used. Base name must be unambiguous per process, e.g. `nessy-<role>-<pid>-<ISO8601 with ':' replaced>`. Call `writeHeapSnapshot(join(dir, base + '.heapsnapshot'))` from `node:v8` (the only new import), then write `join(dir, base + '-diagnostics.json')` containing ONLY counters — `rss`, `heapTotal`, `heapUsed`, `external`, `arrayBuffers`, `unaccountedNative` (rss - heapTotal - external), plus `pid`, `role`, `appVersion`, `uptimeSeconds` — so the Warning at troubleshooting.md:44 holds literally (no session ids, no paths from the workspace, no credentials). Write both with mode 0600. Return `{ snapshotPath, diagnosticsPath, wroteTo: 'desktop' | 'home', bytes }`.

blastRadius: Crosses a wire boundary and a subprocess protocol — both risk triggers under AGENTS.md's verification budget. (1) The new `'server:heapdump'` string enters `RPC_CHANNELS` (packages/shared/src/protocol/channels.ts) which is frozen by apps/electron/src/shared/__tests__/ipc-channels.test.ts:358-372 against an auto-generated list plus a count; regenerate with scripts/ipc-inventory.ts. (2) Routing: adding it to `REMOTE_ELIGIBLE_CHANNELS` (packages/shared/src/protocol/routing.ts:243-252) means a remote-workspace client can make a remote host write files to that host's Desktop — the result object must therefore name role/pid, and the UI copy must not imply the files are local. (3) The Pi host<->subprocess protocol: `InboundMessage` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:302-336) is consumed by the dispatch switch at :4227-4342 and produced by packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts; a packaged host paired with an older Pi bundle must degrade to 'host-only dump' rather than hang, so `requestHeapdump` needs its own timeout (the `get_context_usage` precedent at pi-agent.ts:6030-6047 already has one) and the switch's default branch must stay tolerant. (4) `HeapdumpResultV1` lands in packages/core/src/types (index.ts:84 re-export) which both server and clients import. (5) i18n: new keys must exist in en.json and ru.json or `lint:i18n:parity`/`lint:i18n:sorted` fail. (6) Privacy/filesystem boundary: the writer creates files OUTSIDE any workspace root, so it must be host code — not a supervised process; packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:131-135 rejects a working directory outside the workspace, and routing a heapdump through that path would fail by design. The snapshot is credential-bearing, so mode 0600 and the 'share only -diagnostics.json' wording are part of the contract, not polish. (7) Not a session/persistence write: nothing touches session storage or ~/.nessy/dp_auth_creds.json.
userImpact: Today a user whose Nessy Desktop climbs into the gigabytes has no way to produce a shareable artifact. The `/` menu shows fourteen feature commands and none concerns process memory (`/memory` opens session MEMORY.md); `nessy-general-agent --help` lists no memory command and `doctor` reports configuration only; the Debug menu that could host one is compiled out of packaged builds (apps/electron/src/main/menu.ts:193 `!app.isPackaged`). The three counters we do compute (`server:getStatus`) are never rendered — the Settings server page reads the unrelated `settings:getServerStatus` — so even the numbers are invisible. Practical consequence: a memory report from a real user can only say 'it got slow', and nobody can tell JS-heap growth from native growth, or tell the Electron main apart from the Pi subprocess. Nothing breaks until someone tries to diagnose a leak; the moment they do, the documented recovery step simply does not exist.
